stories.name: AI spending bubble
stories.blurb: Growing concerns that the massive AI infrastructure spending boom is outpacing real returns and increasingly relies on debt, raising fears of a market correction.

stories.name: Meta earnings outlook
stories.blurb: Investors and analysts are weighing Meta Platforms' quarterly earnings, AI spending, and valuation to decide whether the stock is a buy, hold, or sell.

stories.name: Meta Muse AI agent
stories.blurb: Meta's new Muse AI agent has sparked a sharp rally in Meta stock as investors and analysts bet it could become a major competitive threat to Google and a landmark AI product.

stories.name: Meta Pixelworks VR partnership
stories.blurb: Pixelworks is partnering with Meta to bring TrueCut Motion cinematic content to Meta's newly launched VR glasses.

stories.name: AI chip competition
stories.blurb: Tech companies like Meta are diversifying their AI chip suppliers and shifting orders among Nvidia, AMD, and others amid surging demand and supply constraints.

stories.name: Fund Portfolio Moves
stories.blurb: A series of reports tracking which stocks major hedge funds and asset managers bought or sold in their latest portfolio disclosures.

past.name: Meta teen safety settlement
past.blurb: Meta is settling a landmark multistate lawsuit over claims that Facebook and Instagram were designed to be addictive to minors, agreeing to pay billions and overhaul its platforms for teen users.

past.name: Meta AI turnaround
past.blurb: Meta's stock is surging as the company transforms from an AI laggard into a leader, with its AI push reshaping advertising, wearables, and data center plans.

past.name: Big Tech Earnings Week
past.blurb: Investors are watching a busy week of corporate earnings from major technology companies, including Meta, for signals about the market's direction.

past.name: Meta AI supplier investments
past.blurb: Meta is raising roughly $95 billion for its AI buildout while key chip suppliers Nvidia, AMD, and Broadcom invest billions in the company, raising circular-financing concerns.

past.name: Meta's AI Power Play
past.blurb: Meta is making governance, financial, and product moves—from non-voting stock to enterprise AI and subscriptions—to fund its AI buildout while keeping Mark Zuckerberg in control.

past.name: Meta price target hikes
past.blurb: Multiple Wall Street analysts are raising their price targets on Meta Platforms stock while maintaining bullish ratings.

past.name: Meta's Muse AI Agent
past.blurb: Meta launched Muse, its first personal AI agent and coding assistant, as part of a broader push into AI to compete with OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google while facing scrutiny over privacy and safety.

past.name: Digital Ad Stock Watch
past.blurb: Coverage of how Meta's social-media and ad-tech peers—Pinterest, Snap, Reddit, and AppLovin—are performing in the market amid shifts in advertising demand and user growth.

past.name: Meta's AI data center buildout
past.blurb: Meta is spending tens of billions of dollars building massive AI data centers across the U.S. and Canada, often through joint ventures like its partnership with BlackRock.

past.name: AI safety and regulation
past.blurb: Tech companies and governments are grappling with how to regulate and ensure the safety of increasingly powerful AI models amid rapid releases and high-profile incidents.

past.name: MongoDB CEO exit
past.blurb: MongoDB's CEO unexpectedly left to join Meta, raising questions about the company's strategy and sending its stock sharply lower.

past.name: Meta enterprise AI push
past.blurb: Meta is building out an enterprise AI platform and the infrastructure to support it, hiring MongoDB's CEO to lead the unit and striking major data center and monetization deals.

past.name: AI Stock Rally
past.blurb: A broad rally in AI-related stocks, including Meta, AMD, and semiconductor companies, is driving major market gains and record highs amid growing enthusiasm for artificial intelligence technology.

past.name: Meta AI cloud business
past.blurb: Meta is reportedly building a cloud computing business to sell its excess AI compute capacity, positioning itself as a rival to AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud.

past.name: Meta Power Deals
past.blurb: Meta's contracts with energy companies like Vistra and Cogentrix to secure electricity for its data centers are fueling investor interest in power and nuclear-related stocks.

6.text: AI spending concerns are mounting as investors like Hank Paulson and Daniel Loeb warn of overinvestment, with 52% of fund managers expecting a hyperscaler capex cut within six months. Nvidia's leadership crisis and midterm elections have amplified AI stock selloffs, though some analysts see Alphabet's cloud spending as undervalued.

8.text: Meta beat Q3 estimates with $7.40 EPS and $64.6B revenue (up 26% YoY), but a $9.89B legal settlement, negative cash flow, and paused Class C shares weighed on the stock. Shares fell about 8% over the month, short interest jumped 165%, and JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley cut price targets while keeping Overweight ratings.

14.text: Meta's Muse AI agent launched in the UK with retail partners including JD Sports and Marks & Spencer, and is reportedly negotiating Amazon shopping access. Meta also plans a $300 Muse Charm with Verizon 5G, while Apple and Google develop rival agents.

23.text: Australia’s internet safety bill would fine Google and Meta billions for addictive features, while Meta separately urged a controlled approach to AI limits as OpenAI pushed industry standards. Other articles focus on Apple’s agent plans, Trump’s AI policies, and Sheryl Sandberg’s UK AI role.

24.text: Virtuix reported 21% revenue growth and 105% Omni One growth, citing momentum from its Meta partnership; the other three articles (Aramark, Stemtech, Monroe Capital) do not mention Meta.

25.text: Meta is shifting its server chip strategy, potentially benefiting Nvidia, while Meta and Microsoft are maintaining server CPU orders, which could lift AMD and Intel. GF Securities projects a $211 billion AI server market.

26.text: Multiple hedge funds and asset managers disclosed new or increased Meta Platforms positions in Q3 13F filings, including funds managing $15.85B, $22B, $3.2B, $12.97B, $6.6B, $6.5B, and $92.71B. Meta was the largest holding for one $12.97B fund and among the top three for others.

7.text: Meta suspended its plan to issue new Class C non-voting shares amid shareholder lawsuits alleging Zuckerberg pressured the board to preserve control. Internal documents also show its "school communities" push was used to sign teens up for Instagram, while Taiwan flagged China-linked fake accounts and Turkey's antitrust watchdog scrutinized Meta.

17.text: Nvidia denied considering rehiring Jensen Huang, Blackstone bought Amazon data centers, and Apple launched a health study. Meta is not mentioned, so the articles do not bear on it.
